Commentary.Commentary: Keshav Maharaj picked up three wickets, and looking at the spin that he got, Moeen would be licking his fingers. Morris picked up two but was too expensive to the skipper's liking. Stokes and Bairstow just toyed with his bowling. 492-run chase may well be about match-saving for South Africa, but would they be able to sustain for about 140 overs? Join us in a while to find out.

The nagging question  'when would England declare?' is solved finally - now, with 491 runs on the board. For most parts of this session, it seemed more of an ODI than a Test. The English batsmen had their slog modes on. The South African bowlers brought in their change of pace variations but were still hit around the park. Bairstow combined first with Stokes to strike up a quick 49-run stand, and then with Roland-Jones for another brisk 48-run partnership. Root, Westley and Bairstow scored clinical fifties.

OUT! Bairstow holes out! Low full toss on off, Jonny clears his front leg and lifts it towards long off. He has not got enough power behind it and the ball flies towards Rabada who is stationed there. He catches it with both hands at first but then fumbles. The ball pops out and he slips as well but he is aware. Recovers well to grab it with his left hand. Finally, Root feels that England have enough on the board and signals for the DECLARATION! TEA HAS ALSO BEEN TAKEN!
Flatter and quicker, dragged to long on for a single.
Tossed up delivery, spinning away. Bairstow backs away and plays it to sweeper cover for a single.
Coming in with the arm, Roland-Jones whips it through backward square leg for a run.
Floated delivery, punched to extra cover.
Comes down the track and plays it to long off for a single.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
SIX! Tossed up delivery, Toby kneels and tonks it over long on for a biggie. England are surely aiming for the 500 run-mark lead.
Knocked through mid off. A run taken.
Roland-Jones uses his feet and takes it on the full. Slogs it to long on for a single.

SIX! He is showing that he has the capability to impress with the bat. He started his career as a batsman when he was very young. Tossed up delivery, Roland-Jones slog sweeps it with authority over deep square leg for a maximum.
Tossed up delivery, tapped to covers.
Fullish delivery, eased to long off for a single.
Bairstow eases this one through covers for a run. He is struggling a bit. Seems to be having an issue with his ankle.
SIX! Shot! Tossed up delivery, Bairstow kneels and slog sweeps it over deep square leg for a maximum.
Floated delivery on leg, Bairstow goes for the sweep but gets it off the inside edge. The ball lobs over the keeper and just evades the saw dust. Two runs taken.
Elgar is tending to his injured right hand middle finger with the Protea physio's aid.
Tossed up delivery, eased to long on for a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They manage to come back for the second.
16th Test fifty for Bairstow.

FOUR! Brings up his half fifty in style! Tossed up delivery, Bairstow kneels and reverse sweeps it through short third man to find the fence. It is been an enterprising knock from him, takes the lead to 460 with that.
Roland-Jones comes down the track and drags it through wide mid on for a run.
Floated delivery, Jonny uses his feet and jams it towards Elgar. It is hit hard and Dean looks to stop it. It bursts through his hands and goes to long on. A run taken. He seems to have hurt himself.
Tossed up delivery, reverse swept to backward point.
Bairstow uses his feet and milks it down to wide long off. Two runs taken.
Cut towards backward point this time.

Close shave! Coming in with the arm. Roland-Jones uses his feet and gets into a tangle. Ends up getting a nick behind. It goes past de Kock who is blinded a bit. Faf at first slip leaps but fails to take it. The wicket-keeper runs after it, taking his helmet off. Keeps the batsmen down to a couple.
Stays back and defends it.
Flatter delivery, knocked down to long on for a single. The lead touches 450 now.
Shortish delivery, punched through cover-point for a single.
Fullish delivery, wristed through wide mid on for a single.
Fullish delivery on middle, Toby comes down the track and checks his drive towards Elgar. It carries to him on the bounce.
Floated delivery, kept out watchfully.
Uses his feet and taps it down the track.
Tossed up delivery, Bairstow sweeps it uppisly towards deep square leg. Rabada runs to his right but the ball falls short of him. A run taken.
Roland-Jones eases this one to long on for a run.
Tossed up ball, clipped to backward square leg for a single.
Well, well! Dean Elgar to bowl his left arm orthodox now.
Fullish delivery, eased through mid off for a single.
Pushed to covers this time.
Plays this one with an open face to backward point.
Tossed up delivery, defended off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Toby Roland-Jones comes out to bat.

OUT! Great piece of work from Temba Bavuma! Fullish delivery, Bairstow turns it to mid-wicket and sets off for a run. Maharaj himself runs after it. The batsmen sense that there is a couple on offer and attempt it. However, Bavuma in the deep runs in swiftly and attacks the ball. He has one stump to aim at and he hurls an accurate throw. Ali is struggling to reach as the ball brushes the wicket and the bails come off. South Africa appeal and it is referred upstairs. The replays roll in. They show that Ali's bat is just short of the crease as the bails come off. From a few angles, it is confirmed so. Moeen Ali has to depart.
There is a run out appeal against Ali. Seems close and the Proteas are confident.
England bat on, Keshav Maharaj to bowl now.
Fullish delivery, hit to long on for a single.
If England want to field before Tea, they have to declare after this delivery.
Length delivery around off, Bairstow looks to tonk it over mid-wicket but gets beaten completely. Declaration batting going on at the moment.
Back of a length delivery, cut to backward point.
In the air... but safe! Good length delivery on off, Ali has a wild slog across the line but gets a top edge towards deep backward point. Thankfully, it falls short of the fielder. Two runs taken.
FOUR! Poor delivery and taken full toll of! Straying on the pads, Ali manages to get a fine tickle on it and the ball rolls to the fine leg fence.
On a length outside off, steered to third man for a run.
Stays back and taps it to gully for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Bairstow looks to dab it but gets it off the outer half to third man. Two runs taken.
Fullish delivery, driven to mid off for a quick single. Ali is off the mark.
Moeen Ali is the next man in. Yes, you read it right! The declaration isn't here yet. England continue to bat on.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Stokes sacrifices his wicket for the cause of his side. Slower good length delivery on middle, stays a bit low. Stokes goes for the pull but is early into the shot. Misses it altogether to see the furniture behind him get shattered. He has done his job by helping himself to a breezy knock. England lead by 429 runs.

Seems that it was a passing shower, as the umbrellas in the stands have been closed. It has also become brighter out there. Talking about brightness, things at the moment are looking bright for the Englishmen, but not so for the African team!
Length delivery around off, punched hard to extra cover.
SIX! That's a mighty hit from the big man! Fuller length ball on middle, Stokes with a high backlift heaves it over deep mid-wicket. He has struck it nicely and the ball clears the fence with ease.
Length delivery outside off, dabbed towards deep backward point again. Good running between the wickets allows the batsmen to come back for the second.

The talk on air is about declaration. Shane Warne feels 425-430 runs are enough. Nasser Hussain feels that England should have a go at the Proteas with the ball, before tea. He also felt 450 would be an ideal lead to have.
Short delivery, pulled to deep backward square leg for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Slower short delivery down the leg side, Bairstow looks to help it but misses.

Good length delivery outside off, tapped through backward point. The batsmen take on the fielder. The throw is at striker's end as Bairstow goes to the danger end. He fails to collect it cleanly. Two safely taken in the end.
Bairstow looks to play it square of the wicket on the off side but ends up chopping it beside the pitch.
While in his followthrough, the ball slips out of Rabada's hand. The batsman ran across towards it and sees the funny side of it. Rabada has a wry smile on his face.
Fullish delivery, Bairstow pushes at it but gets it off the inner half to backward square leg. A run taken.
The batsman plays the square cut.
FOUR! This is class batting! Shortish delivery outside off, Bairstow waits for it and guides it late to the third man boundary.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Angling into Bairstow. He clips it through fine leg to find the fence.
Fuller length ball angling across Ben. He attempts a wild hit through the line but it seems to have gone over extra cover as the cameras show so. However, it has gone down to third man. A run taken.
Rain is in the air as the sight of umbrellas opening up in the crowd suggests!
Fullish delivery, Stokes uses his feet and drills it to mid on.

FOUR! Innovation at its best! Root plays this shot really well. Jonny has taken inspiration from his skipper it seems. Shortish delivery angling into Bairstow. He arches back and ramps it over the keeper's head for a boundary.
Warne wants some of the popcorn that the small boy among the spectators is seen having! Yummy!!
Length delivery angling across the southpaw. Placed to deep point for a single.

Jagging in from outside off, Jonny looks to keep it out but gets a thick inside edge to backward square leg. Bairstow pushes for the second but the fielder is quick to attack the ball. The batsmen settle for a single.
Fullish delivery outside off, eased towards wide mid off.
Two Leg byes! Going down the leg side, Bairstow looks to clip it but misses. The ball brushes his pads and rolls to fine leg. Two leg byes taken.
On a length outside off, Stokes flays it through cover-point for a single.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! The lead swells to 398. The Proteas will be worried. Angling into Bairstow. He clips it nicely through square leg and the ball races to the fence.

FOUR! Streaky but effective! On a fuller length outside off, Bairstow flashes at it and flashes hard. Gets it off the outer half towards gully. Kuhn stationed there leaps to his right like a goal keeper but the ball goes past him in a jiffy. A boundary results.
Outside off, dabbed to gully.
Good length delivery jagging back sharply. Bairstow is caught in the crease as he looks to play it across but gets hit on the thigh pad. No such appeal as height was a factor.
Going down the leg side, Bairstow looks to whip it across but misses.
Full length delivery around off, Stokes drives it to long on for a single.
Very full on off, targeting the off stick. Jonny does well to jam it back towards Rabada.
Back of a length outside off, played with an open face to gully.
Fuller in length outside off, Bairstow pushes at it tentatively but gets it off the inner half to mid-wicket. Wants a run but it is not there on offer.

Rabada loses his radar and slips this one down the leg side, Bairstow fails to clip it. De Kock dives to his left and fails to gather it cleanly. Amla at first slip is alert and goes across quickly to the ball to deny the single.
Well-directed short delivery, climbing on Stokes. He is hurried a touch and ends up top edging his pull safely to fine leg. A run taken.
Fullish delivery in line of the stumps, driven crisply to mid on.
Time for Drinks. England have taken the lead to 388 and a declaration seems to be around the corner. Stokes might choose to unleash himself completely now.
Very full ball outside off, Bairstow tries to get bat to that and misses.
Length ball on middle and leg, Stokes inside edges it on to his pads. They take a single as the ball rolls just past the stumps towards fine leg.
The full ball on off and middle is defended showing the full face of the bat.
Length ball outside off, played off the back foot for a single.
Shortish ball just outside off, Stokes cuts that away to deep point for a run.

Length ball just outside off and swinging away, Bairstow pokes his bat at that to defend. The ball takes the outside edge and lands just short of a diving du Plessis at second slip. They cross over for a run. The first slip fielder has a shy at the striker's end and manages to hit the bull's eye, but the batsman was well in.
Leg stump line, turned around the corner for a single.
Good length delivery angling in sharply. Bairstow camps back and defends it to the right side of Rabada.
Similar length delivery outside off, placed to gully.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Jonny punches it towards covers where the fielder fumbles a bit and the ball goes through. Two runs taken.
Going down the leg side, Bairstow looks to clip it across but is hit on the thigh pad.
Starts off with a delivery on the pads, Stokes helps it through mid-wicket for a single.
Rabada to bowl another spell now.
Length ball outside off and swinging away, Bairstow shoulders arms.
Jonny Bairstow walks in at the fall of the 5th wicket.

OUT! YES HE'S GOT HIM! That was a back of length ball that started on middle and shaped into the batsman. Malan misses the flick and gets hit on the pads. The Proteas appeal only to see it turned down by umpire Wilson. Faf reviews that immediately, and boy, what a review that is! There was no bat on that, and the Ball Tracker returned three reds for the LBW call. This means the end of Malan's stay. As he played that shot, he seems to fall over, in sort of a similar way like he did in the first innings. England 5 down now. They lead by 380!
Faf du Plessis has immediately reviewed an LBW decision against Malan. Seems close to the naked eye.
FOUR! EDGED AND FOUR! Morris bowls it back of a length on off and draws Malan's bat. The ball takes the outside edge and crawls away through the slip cordon and into the third man fence.
Length ball outside off, stokes punches that off the back foot through covers. Morkel chases that down and saves a run for their side.
Short ball on middle, pulled away to square leg.
Full ball flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Chris Morris is back on.
Length ball in line of the stumps, defended from the crease.
Length ball played from within the crease.
Played to the point region by the batsman for no run.

WHAT'S HAPPENING THERE! Full ball on middle and leg, Stokes tries to flick it but ends up getting a leading edge that goes towards deepish mid off, where Rabada fields and has a shy at the non-striker's end. The ball misses the stumps and evades a diving de Kock and rolls towards short third man. Seeing this, Malan tries to sneak in another run. This attempt for a run makes Morris throw the ball towards the bowler's end, where the ball misses the fielder backing up and goes to Rabada again. Rabada mocks a throw again! The batsman ends up getting just a single off that delivery. All's well that ends well though!
Length ball on off, defended from within the crease.
Full ball on off, Malan tries to flick it and gets a leading edge. The ball rolls towards gully, where a slight misfield allows them a run.
Looped outside off, Stokes goes to defends it and gets hit high on his pads. The ball rolls over towards slip.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fires that on off, Stokes defends.

FOUR! Crunched off the back foot this time! That was flatter outside off and a tad short too, Stokes goes on the back foot and smashes it through wide mid off for a boundary. He is taking a liking to the left arm orthodox bowler here.

IN THE AIR, BUT SAFE! Flighted ball on off and turning into him, Stokes goes for the slog sweep and tried to hit that out of The Oval! He ends up skying that and fortunately for him it lands between mid-wicket and long on. They collect a brace before Rabada, who ran there from mid on, returns the throw.
Deep backward point in place now.

FOUR! Expect such shots when Stokes is in an aggressive mood against a tweaker. Tossed up delivery outside off is an invitation for the big Ben to go for the reverse sweep, and he doesn't disappoint. He crunches it through the point region for a boundary.
Length ball outside off, Malan hangs his bat out but doesn't make any contact with it. Thankfully!
Defended off the front foot by Malan presenting the full face of the bat.
Length ball on off, played towards point for a single.
Hashim Amla is off the field informs Mike Atherton on air. Seems to have hurt his finger as he tried to stop a wide ball in the previous Philander over.
Back of a length ball on middle, blocked off the back foot.
Another length ball defended from the crease by Stokes.
Length ball on middle and off, defended by Stokes from within the crease.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The flight in that ball invites Malan down the track, but he defends it after stepping down the track.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Looped on off and middle, Stokes gets off the mark with a sweep shot.
Fired in around off, Stokes defends showing the full face of the bat.
Tossed up on off and middle, flicked away on the on side for a single.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
That's a length ball on the stumps, played off the back foot.
Another ball outside off left alone.
Fuller ball outside off, driven straight to covers.
The floodlights are switched on. It certainly is getting gloomy out there.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Malan tries to sweep and gets hit on the pad. In a session where England are expected to attack the opposition, a spinner gets in a wicket-maiden! Well bowled!
Loopy ball on off, played towards mid-wicket.
The batsman fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad.
Ben Stokes strides out to the center at No.6. A bit of drizzle is also in the air. It has gone murky and the artificial lights are on as well. Let's hope it goes away.

OUT! Of all the ways to get out in a Test match, this is the one that Root chooses today! Flighted ball on off and spinning away, Root tries to slog sweep it and ends up getting a top edge. The ball flies high up and towards deep square leg, where Morkel gleefully accepts the catch. Root departs as soon as he gets to a landmark, something that he wouldn't like. And in a Test, he gets out in a limited overs fashion! England four down!
Tossed up on middle, he has inside edged that on to his pads.
That's a shortish ball on off, punched off the back foot.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Crashed to get off the mark! That was full on middle and leg, Malan flicks it away off his pads to send the ball rushing into the mid-wicket boundary.
Joe Root gets to his 29th half century in Tests.
Length ball outside off, driven towards backward point for a single to bring up his fifty.
WIDE! That's full wide outswinging delivery, Malan lets it go. De Kock puts in the dive but is unable to stop that as they collect two wides.
That's bowled just outside off, Root drives it to covers for a run.
Length ball around off, he plays it towards point for a brace.
Vernon Philander comes back for a bowl.
Dawid Malan walks in next.

OUT! What great spin bowling! WESTLEY DECEIVED IN FLIGHT! Maharaj tossed it up outside off, invited the batsman down. Tom fell for that as he chipped down, but he couldn't get to the pitch of the ball to account for the spin. The ball spun away and went through to de Kock who did the rest. End of a good knock by the debutant, England lose their third.
Flighted on middle, driven through mid on for a single.
He defends off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy ball outside off, guided to short third man by opening the face of his bat.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Aaah! Misfield from Philander. That was pushed flatter and quicker just outside off, Root cuts it through point. The fielder at cover-point does all the work of getting there and bending to field it. But the ball spins away just that little bit and goes through Vernon and into the point fence.

FOUR! Frustration for South Africa. Back of a length ball just outside off, Westley pokes his bat at that. To his credit, he did so with soft hands. The ball went between gully and the third slip and through to the third man fence. Though it wasn't a boundary ball, England collect four off that!
A tad fuller on off, Tom plays it from within the crease..
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Length ball outside off, punched off the back foot for a run.
That was a tad fuller angled down the leg side, it hits Root low on his pads.
Length ball outside off, Root looks to flay and misses.
Looped on middle, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Flighted on off and middle, defended off the front foot.
Loopy ball on off, played to long off for yet another run.
Fuller ball on off, driven to long off for a run.

FOUR! SHOT! That was pushed flatter around off, but it was a tad short. Westley thrashes it in the gap between short extra cover and short cover and that crashes into the boundary cushions. It is dealt with disdain.
Looped up on middle, Tom drives it towards mid off.
Fuller ball on off, Root gets it off the inner half of his bat on the leg side. Good probing over by Morkel. Another maiden.
Fuller ball outside off, Root looks to push it on the off side, ends up getting an inside edge onto his back pad. On another day, it could have gone on to the stumps.
Back of a length outside off, Root feels for it and gets beaten.
A tad fuller outside off, played to covers.
Fuller ball around off, he gets it off the inside half of the bat towards mid on.
Length ball on off, played off the back foot into the ground.
That's tossed up on off, Root places it with soft hands towards point and sets off for a quick single.
Floated on off, played towards backward point.
Loopy ball just outside off, cut away to point.
That's pushed on a good length on off, defended off the back foot.
Floated on middle and off, defended showing the full face of the bat.
Loopy ball on middle, played to covers.
Keshav Maharaj will continue.
Bouncer but off target. Tom ducks under that as it goes to the keeper. Maiden to start off.
Length outside off, that swung after it passed the batsman. Westley shoulders arms to that.
Angling down the leg side, Westley tries a flick and misses.
Length ball outside off, swinging away, Westley doesn't bother playing that.
Length delivery outside off, moving away after pitching. Westley points his bat skywards to allow it through.

Tom Westley and Joe Root will look to bat with more intent. The English skipper may well decide to declare in this session itself. Shane Warne on air informed that there was a bit of rain during the lunch break but the weather has cleared up now.
Fullish delivery around off, driven crisply to mid off.
...DAY 4, SESSION 2...

It all looks gloomy for the African side and the game is going away from them. Morkel and Rabada have been good but they have been negotiated smartly. Philander has not quite looked his usual self after the illness. The home side will look to bat with more intent going forward. A score of around 400 might be an uphill task for the visitors to chase. Join us in a while for the afternoon session.

Good session for England and they are dictating the terms at the moment. The lead has swelled to 331 runs with still five sessions left in this Test match. The debutant, Westley has been solid and has worked hard to earn his maiden half century. He has got Root for company who has taken the initiative to put away the loose deliveries.
Coming in with the arm, Root pushes at it tentatively but gets it off the inner half to mid-wicket. THAT SHALL BE LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Quick delivery on off, kept out on the off side.
A bit flatter this time, Joe hangs back and pushes it to covers.
Loopy delivery, Joe prods forward and pushes it to the off side.
Tossed up delivery, defended off the front foot.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Another one that is way outside off, left alone again.

Westley has got most of his boundaries towards the on side. That just goes on to show how strong he has been on the leg side. Anything on middle and leg, the ball has only one place to go - the boundary fence!
Good length delivery outside off, seams away after hitting the deck. Westley leaves it alone.
Morkel hits the deck hard but the line is wayward. It is wide outside off. Westley keeps his bat inside the line and ignores it.
This is well outside off, Westley doesn't bother to play at that.
Fuller in length, shaping into Westley. He covers the line and defends it.
Length delivery well outside off, Westley covers his off stump and sees it through.
Loopy delivery, kept out watchfully.
Fullish on middle, eased to mid-wicket.
Deft! A bit short outside off, Root waits for it and guides it past first slip. Picks up a couple to his name.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Floated ball, pushed back to the bowler.
Tossed up delivery, defended off the front foot.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Maiden Test fifty for Tom Westley.

FOUR! What a way to reach his fifty on debut! Well played young man! Fullish delivery angling in sharply to Westley. He clips it authoritatively through mid-wicket and the ball whistles away to the fence. He has a smile on his face and his captain appreciates his effort. It has been a good innings by him.
Morkel gets this one to shape back in on a fullish length. Westley has the line covered and works it to mid-wicket.
Morkel is bowling beautifully! Keeps it outside off and gets it to swing away prodigiously. Westley is again drawn into the drive but gets foxed.
Half-volley outside off, driven crisply towards Bavuma at short cover. He dives to his left to save a certain boundary.
Fuller in length outside off, seaming away after hitting the deck. Westley goes for a drive down the ground but gets beaten.
Morne Morkel is back into the attack.
Tossed up on middle, spinning away. Root drives it to short extra cover. England lead by 325 runs. A great position to be in. They are in the driver's seat.
Fullish delivery, Westley wrists it through wide mid on. Rabada at deepish mid on moves across to his right to stop it. A run taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Root is nimble on his feet and works it through square leg. The batsmen take the single quickly but rightly decide against the second run as the fielder is quick to the ball.
Floated outside off, driven crisply to short extra cover.
Fullish delivery on off, turned to mid-wicket.
Fuller length ball outside off, holding its line. Tom leaves it alone.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, Westley with a bit of an open face drives it through covers. Two runs taken. He moves to 45 with that. He has played a gritty knock so far.
This one swings in sharply from a length outside off, Westley goes for the flick but is hit on the thigh pad.

Nasser Hussain analyses and says that Philander is more dangerous when he seams the bowl rather than swing it. His bowling average supports the views - 46.5 when trying to swing as against 14.6 when trying to bowl seam-up. While he has been wayward in swinging the ball, he is more accurate with seaming deliveries.
Fullish in length outside off, swinging away. Westley plants his front foot across to let it go.
Wide outside off this time, Tom doesn't fiddle with it.
Shortish delivery around the rib cage area. Westley hops back and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Westley works this one with the angle through wide mid on for a run.
Floated in line of the stumps, worked to mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Slow through the air this time, Westley uses his feet and swings across the line but ends up dragging it towards mid-wicket. The fielder dives to his right to stop it.
Turns this with the angle to mid-wicket.
Shortish delivery on off, defended off the back foot.
David Gower on air informs that Chris Morris left the field a few minutes earlier. Not sure of the reason though. Meanwhile, Keshav Maharaj finally gets to bowl.
Beauty! A bit fuller outside off, Root shuffles across to negotiate it but the ball angles in sharply to beat him on the inside.
Outside off, Root lets it go.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Good length delivery just outside off, straightens a touch after pitching. Root has no choice but to play it and is comprehensively beaten.
50-run stand up between Root and Westley.
Fullish ball outside off, Westley goes for an expansive drive but ends up getting it off the outer half to backward point. The fielder dives to his left and makes a good half stop. A run taken.
Full delivery outside off, driven through cover-point for an easy run.

Philander has gone off the field. Meanwhile, Keshav Maharaj comes on for a bowl. Can he break this partnership? But there is a change in plan now. Rabada is called back into the attack. Phehlukwayo is the substitute fielder in Vernon's place.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Length delivery on off, straightens a touch. Westley does well to play it with an angled bat to gully.
Jaffa! On a good length around off coming in with the angle. Westley offers a straight bat in defense but the ball seams away after landing to catch him off guard.
Back of a length outside off, Joe punches it crisply towards cover-point. Elgar dives to his left but the ball sneaks past him. A run taken.
Similar length delivery angling in this time. Joe goes for the clip but is struck on the thigh pad.
Length delivery outside off, tapped to point.
Philander is varying his lines and length nicely. Goes full outside off this time and induces a false stroke. Westley is drawn into the drive but is beaten all ends up due to the away movement.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
That's a beauty and well played in the end! Short of a length around off, shapes away substantially after pitching. Westley follows it initially but manages to bail out at the last moment.

FOUR! Shot! Runs are flowing at the moment! Short of a length outside off and width on this occasion. Westley hangs back and punches it towards backward point. The fielder there dives to his left but the ball goes past him in a jiffy. Another boundary results.
In the channel outside off, left alone.

Back of a length delivery outside off, swinging away. Joe cuts it through point. He is again interested in the second but the fielder is quick to the ball. Returns an accurate throw at the bowler's end which denies the second.
Shortish well outside off, Joe cuts it to deep point for a single and will retain the strike. 11 from the over.

FOUR! Root is not going to miss out on those! Short and width on offer. Root stands tall and cuts it through backward point. Bavuma sprints across to his left and puts in a desperate dive but fails to stop the boundary.
Good length around off, pushed off the back foot to covers.

Morris goes wider of the crease and angles this on substantially. Root is a bit tentative as he pushes at it. Gets a thick inside edge through backward square leg. There is urgency in the running and the skipper calls Westley back for the second. Good running there!
Fuller length ball outside off, shaping away. Root plants his front foot across to allow it through.
FOUR! Well played! Good length delivery angling in sharply, Root hangs back and works it expertly through square leg. The timing is spot on and the ball whistles away to the fence.
A bit of drizzle is in the air. Up go the umbrellas in the crowd. However, it is not dark and hopefully it is a passing shower.
In the channel around off, Westley works it to the man at mid-wicket.
Defended off the back foot by Tom Westley.
Straighter on this occasion, Tom works it to the man at mid-wicket.
Camps back to the length delivery and pushes it beside the bowler on the off side.
Well bowled! Maintains a similar line and length around off. Westley pushes at it tentatively but the ball seams away after hitting the deck to fox him.
Length delivery in the fifth stump channel, Westley hangs back and defends it to covers.

Short and room on offer, the English skipper makes good use of the depth of the crease and punches it through cover-point. Bavuma from deep point comes across, picks it up and throws it back to Morris. Good running between the batsmen allows them to take a couple.
Goes back to the good length delivery and dabs it to the man at gully.
pushed off the front foot to the off side.
Shortish delivery outside off, Root shapes to play it behind square on the off side but the inward angle suprises him a bit. He gets cramped up and only manages to chop it to widish first slip.
Back of a length on off, defended solidly off the back foot.
Morris goes wide of the crease and angles in a length delivery from outside off. Root stays back and blocks it to short cover.
Another outswinger outside off which is left alone by Westley.
Pitched further up outside off, swinging away. It evokes no interest from Tom.
Back of a length delivery on off, Westley uses the depth of the crease and plays it with an angled blade to gully.
Good length delivery sliding down leg, Westley looks to play it through but is hit on the thigh pad.
In the zone outside off, Tom doesn't fiddle with it.
Good length delivery around off, Westley camps back and taps it to short cover.

The first hour of the day has led to the umps calling for Drinks! England have swelled the lead to 299 runs and are scoring runs at a fair clip. They would look to maintain the pressure on the visitors. On the other hand, the Proteas need something heroic to stay in the contest.

FOUR! GLORIOUS, GRACIOUS, GORGEOUS! That's a perfect cover drive. It is a full ball outside off, Root gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through covers. Bavuma runs from deep cover-point to covers in a hope to get to the ball before it reaches the fence, but it is not to be. That was timed perfectly!
That's a length ball outside off, tapped towards cover-point for a quick single.
Length ball on middle and off, Westley gets a leading edge back to the bowler.
That's fuller and wide of off, left alone.
Length ball on middle, flicked away towards mid-wicket for a run.
That's bowled full outside off, left alone.
Chris Morris into the attack.

David Gower on air analyses Westley's skills. As Westley got out by trying to play a ball on off towards leg, his practice session was done keeping in mind that. The coach was seen bowling under-arms to him outside off and Tom tried to play it in the area from mid off to cover-point, consciously trying to not play towards the on side.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
A tad fuller ball on off, played off the front foot and into the ground.
That's a good length ball outside off, punched away to covers.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Length ball on off, punched off the back foot.
Full outside off, Root drives it crisply to cover-point for a single. That short deserved more than a run.
Yorker on off, dug out by Westley.
FOUR! That's driven wonderfully well, and the batsman has maintained his balance. It's on a length on off angling into him, he plays it through mid on and into the fence.
As a part of charity, some caricatures of the ex-cricketers are up for auction there. Warne on air suggests Pollock to auction his cartoon at 27 million pounds!
That's flicked away on the leg side straight to the fielder.
Fuller ball in the line of the stumps, defended from with the crease.
Length ball on off, defended from within the crease. That seems to have stayed a touch low.
Short ball on off and middle, pulled away to fine leg for a single.
That's bowled on off and middle, defended from within the crease.
That's on a length around off, punched away on the off for a run.
Back of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
That's bowled on middle, played to mid-wicket.
Fuller on off, driven towards mid on.

FOUR! Well played skip! That's bowled on a length just outside off, Root opens the face of the bat at the last moment and guides it from between the third slip and gully. The ball races away to the third man fence.
Vernon Philander into the attack.
That's a tad fuller around off, Tom gets an inside edge that rolls to the keeper as he pokes his bat at that.
That's full down the leg side, he misses his flick.
That's a good length ball just outside off, draws Westley forward who misses it.
Length ball outside off, punched away towards point for a run.
FOUR! That's bowled a tad fuller on middle and leg, flicked away towards deep mid-wicket for a boundary. The big Vern gave it a chase from mid on, yet couldn't cut that off.
Speared in on a length outside off, punched off the back foot back to the bowler..
A tad fuller on off, defended showing the full face.
Length ball outside off, Westley points his bat skywards and lets it go.
Length ball outside off, driven square on the off side for a single.
That's bowled on a length on off, defended off the back foot.

Aah! Peach! Root escapes. That's on a back of a length around off, Root gets beaten on the inside. Previously, the balls were moving away, but this one came in and caught him unawares. The ball didn't miss the edge and the off stump by much.
Length ball outside off, left alone by the skipper.
Root gets going! That's a full ball outside off, he drives it to deep cover-point for a run.
Length ball on off, defended from within the crease.
A tad fuller on off, pushed towards covers.
That's seamed just outside off, Root fails to get bat on that.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Root.
Length ball on middle and leg, pushed towards mid on.
Length ball on off and middle, it strikes him high on his pads.
WIDE! Aptly described on air by Nasser Hussain as 'easily his worst ball'. That was an attempted bouncer, but way outside off and over the batsman's head. Wide signaled.
That's bowled outside off, shouldered arms to by the batsman.
Yet another bouncer on off and middle, Westley ducks under that.
Short outside off, Westley thinks of pulling and leaves it later.
Bouncer on off, Westley evades that.
Length ball on middle, flicked to mid-wicket.

Since the start of play today, the Proteas were feeding Jennings with fuller and good length balls. The one that got him was the short one. Atherton makes a nice point on air. He says that if you want to surprise the batsman with a bouncer, it'd better be on the batsman in the line of the stumps, for it to be effective. That's what's consumed Jennings today.
Bowled on a good length outside off, played towards point.
Good yorker on off, dug out by Root.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Good length ball outside off, Westley drives it through covers where Kuhn chases that. As he slides to save it, he slips again due to the wet outfield, and that allows them three runs.
Length ball outside off, Westley leaves that one.
That's good judgement shown by the batsman. Length ball just outside off, left alone.
Root doesn't play that length ball outside off.
That's bowled on middle and leg, flicked away on the leg side.
Back of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Root.
Length ball on middle and leg, flicked away to the leg side for a run.
Length ball on off, played off the inner half to the on side..
The English skipper, Joe Root walks in next.

OUT! EXCELLENT STUFF BY RABADA! He set Jennings up wonderfully well there. The entire over he kept bowling it fuller and outside off. Jennings had a play and a miss on the previous ball. This time he surprises the batsman with a good short ball on middle and off. The opener jabs his bat at that only to glove the ball, which goes in the air to gully where Morris takes a jumping catch. Terrific strategy there. Jennings departs without a well deserved fifty. England two down!
That's bowled in the corridor of uncertainty outside off, Jennings tries playing at that buts ends up missing the ball.
Another length ball outside off, he leaves it alone.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Length ball on middle and leg, played to mid on.
Length ball outside off, left alone.

Much better shot this time. Full ball outside off, Jennings drives it through covers. Kuhn chases it from mid off and as he slides to stop the ball, the wet outfield makes him slide a couple of yards further leaving the ball behind. He is successful in saving a run though.

FOUR! Streaky runs, but runs nevertheless. Good length ball around off, Jennings tries to push it towards covers. He ends up getting an outside edge that runs to the right of a diving Bavuma at backward point and rushes away slowly to the boundary. The outfield seems pretty slow owing to the incessant rains yesterday.
Back of a length ball on middle and going towards leg, it hits the batter high on his pads as he misses his flick.
Fuller ball on off, Keaton edges that towards the gully region.
That's speared in on a length, he gets an inside edge and the ball thuds on to his pads.

FOUR! That's the first boundary of the day with the bat! Length ball just outside off, Keaton pushes his bat to block that delivery. The ball takes the outside edge and runs away for a boundary between the slips and the gully.
A defensive shot off the full face of the bat to that length ball on off.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Aah! Length ball outside off, inviting the drive. England's position in the match allows him to go for his shots, and hence he goes for it, only to see the ball whiz past the edge.
That's bowled on off and middle, defended from within the crease.
Length ball on off, blocked off the back foot.
Nasser Hussain on air informs that Philander cannot bowl immediately as he was out of the field for most of the time yesterday.
Full ball on middle and leg, flicked away towards wide mid on for a single.
Length ball on off, played off the back foot.
Fuller ball on off, driven straight back to the bowler.
Length ball outside off, Tom doesn't bother playing that.
Length ball around off, driven away to covers.
50 partnership up between Jennings and Westley.
Length ball on off and middle, flicked away for a run.
Starts with a full ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Morne Morkel to bowl from the other end.
FOUR LEG BYES! Back of a length ball starting on middle and going down leg, Westley tries to flick it. The ball takes his thigh pads and runs away to the fine leg fence for a boundary.

That's bowled on middle and angling into the batsman. Westley tries to push it towards mid on, instead he gets an inside edge and the ball strikes his pads. It draws an appeal for LBW by the visitors, rightfully turned down by the umpire.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, flicked away towards backward square leg. First runs for the day.
Starts off with a full length ball outside off that zips through to the keeper.

The players and the umpires step on the field. Keaton Jennings to face the first ball of the day from Kagiso Rabada, who will complete the pending over. Tom Westley is at the non-striker's end. Two slips and a gully to start with.

Hello and a warm welcome to the fourth day's play of the third Test between England and South Africa. Rains felt ignored and yesterday decided to draw all the attention to them by not allowing play since an hour after lunch. We can only hope that they stay away today and let the Sunday crowd witness an exciting contest between bat and ball. 98 overs of play should be possible today, if weather permits. Stay with us.
... DAY FOUR, SESSION ONE ...

The forecast for tomorrow is a bit better and we all hope that the weather holds up. A score of around 400 will be an uphill task to chase in the overcast English conditions. Join us tomorrow for Day 4 at 1100 local (1000 GMT). Till then, goodbye and cheers!

England hold the aces at the moment as they have swelled the lead to 252 runs with still 9 wickets in hand. Westley and Jennings will look to come out tomorrow and bat with intent to put more pressure on the Proteas. It will require a herculean effort on the part of the visitors to stay in the contest. They will bank on the trio of Rabada, Philander and Morkel to pick up wickets. However, the fitness of Philander is still a concern.
1715 LOCAL TIME UPDATE - The rain has played spoilsport to ruin the day. The umpires have decided that it is enough. THAT'S STUMPS ON DAY 3!

1640 LOCAL TIME UPDATE - Live scenes from the ground are not that great. Though the rain has lightened up, it still looks very gloomy. The umpires have been spotted with their umbrellas. The groundsmen are doing the mopping up work but the covers are still firmly in place. There is an OFFICIAL INSPECTION scheduled to take place at 1730 local time.
1610 LOCAL TIME UPDATE - News from the ground is that TEA HAS BEEN TAKEN. Let's hope that the rain relents.
1510 LOCAL TIME UPDATE - It's very gloomy out there and the rain is getting harder. Doesn't seem that play would be resuming shortly. Stay with us more updates.

1445 LOCAL TIME UPDATE - The clouds have settled in and the rain has set in as well. The umpires call for the covers to be brought in and out come the groundsmen running with them. The players walk off the field at a leisurely pace. The evening forecast is not that great but let's keep our fingers crossed as the English weather is quite unpredictable! We all are hoping that it doesn't turn out to be a lengthy delay. Stay tuned with us for more updates...
Length delivery, a bit of extra bounce on that as it angles away from Keaton. He points his bat skywards to allow it through.
The rain has got heavier. The groundsmen are ready with the covers.
Fuller length ball angling in from outside off, tapped to covers.

Time for Drinks. It has been an absorbing hour of play with both sides doing well. The initial highlight was that Morkel worked Cook out to send him packing. After that, Westley has looked compact while Jennings is also keeping the scoreboard ticking. There have been times when both have been caught off guard but they have managed to battle through it. They have taken the lead to 252. Rabada has bowled with intent and is in the midst of a good spell. South Africa will want him to provide a few breakthroughs.
Good length delivery angling in sharply, Westley hops back to work it across but is pinged on the back thigh.
Straying on the pads, clipped to deep backward square leg for a run.
Well bowled! In the channel outside off, Jennings is drawn into the drive but the ball seams away to beat him.
Length delivery going down the leg side, Keaton goes for the flick but misses.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Length delivery angling in from outside off, Jennings make use of the depth of the crease to block it.
On a length, Tom hangs back and defends it. Three maidens in a row for Rabada, superb stuff!

That's a jaffa! Fullish delivery outside off, Westley committs to the drive down the ground but the ball swings away late to fox him completely. In the first innings, he had got out attempting a similar shot. He needs to be careful.
Fullish delivery, flicked to mid-wicket.
Westley stops Rabada in his followthrough. He was not ready perhaps. Meanwhile, a few umbrellas go up in the crowd.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Westley stays back and plays it with a closed bat face to mid-wicket.
In the zone outside off, swings in after pitching. Tom lets it go.
Back of a length outside off, Westley plays it with an angled bat towards gully. He intercepts and gets a hand to it to take the pace off the ball. A run taken.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Flashes and flashes hard! Short and room on offer, Westley cuts it late. Gets it past backward point and the ball races to the fence.
Good length delivery wide outside off, swings further away. Tom shuffles across and leaves it alone.
On a length outside off, Westley leaves it alone.
FOUR! Westley is looking in great touch! Fractionally overpitched outside off, Tom creams it through extra cover for an elegant boundary.
Chris Morris is into the attack.
Good delivery! Yorker outside off, Jennings does well to jam it out.
Well-directed short delivery on middle, Keaton sits under the bumper.
Good length delivery around leg stump, Jennings hops and looks to defend it but is hit on the back pad. A muted appeal from Rabada is turned down.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Length delivery, shaping away after pitching. Jennings points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Stays back and defends the length delivery.
Full length delivery, driven hard through wide mid on. Two runs taken.
Outside off, left alone.
Dug in short, Tom ducks under it.
Fullish on off, defended off the front foot.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fullish delivery, shaping away. Westley feels for it but gets beaten.

NOT OUT! Jennings survives! Good length delivery around leg stump, Jennings is caught in the crease as he looks to keep it out but misses. The ball brushes the flap of his front pad and then pings him on the back thigh. It then carries to de Kock. A confident appeal follows and the umpire Joel Wilson rules him out but we are not sure of the reason why he decides to do so. Jennings walks across and has a chat with Westley. He decides to challenge the decision. Time for the replays. They first check for the inside edge. There is clear daylight between bat and ball. Time for the Hawk Eye. It shows that it is pitching outside leg and that is the end of the story. It also shows that it would have gone over the stumps. Good use of the review.

Keaton Jennings after a chat with his partner opts to take the review against an LBW decision. Pollock on air informs that there might be two sounds. So if there is an edge, he will be out caught behind.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Good length on leg, with a bit of extra bounce. Jennings defends it tentatively.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length outside off, dabbed to point.
Well bowled! Length delivery on off, shapes away after pitching. Jennings keeps his bat inside the line to let it go.
FOUR! Textbook stuff! Full length ball outside off, Westley leans forward and drives it elegantly through mid off to find the fence.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Fuller in length and angling into Keaton. He pushes at it tentatively but gets a thick inside edge to fine leg. A run taken.
On a length outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Straying on the pads, Jennings clips it through square leg to find the fence.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball on leg, flicked away towards fine leg for a single. Not the greatest of ways to start an over by Rabada as he has conceded 9 off it.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! Length ball on middle and off, crunched through cover-point off the back foot. The fielder at point and mid off try to chase that, but they can't.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Short and wide, the ball had only one place to go - the point boundary! Jennings just smashed that ball through the off side, nobody stood a chance of stopping that.
Starts over the wicket, he bowls it short on middle and leg, Jennings punches it off the back foot to point.
Kagiso Rabada in to bowl now as Philander is off the field as mentioned by Pollock on air.
Full ball on off, driven to mid on. No run there.
Straight length ball outside off, Westley doesn't fiddle with that.
Back of a length ball on middle, played towards fine leg for a run.
Slanting fuller ball on off and middle, played towards mid-wicket. This one wasn't too far from hitting the pad first.
Similar ball outside off, KJ doesn't bother playing that.
Full length ball on off and middle, Jennings shows the full face of the bat and defends.
Length ball outside off, left alone. Two boundaries in the over.
Tome lets that ball outside the stumps go through.
FOUR! Poor ball, punished! That's bowled back of a length on middle angling down leg, Tom just has to help it away which he does. The ball is in a hurry to get to the fine leg fence.
Another length ball outside off, well left.

FOUR! A tad fuller on off, with a slight movement away. Westley covers the line and drives it down the ground for a scintillating boundary. This young lad isn't shy in going for his shots at the big stage, which is good.
Outswinging length ball just outside off, Westley watches it carefully and leaves it alone.
Full ball on off, played towards point.
Full ball on off, almost like the one that got Cook. Keaton tries to play it towards the on side and misses the ball. This one just passes over the off pole!
Length ball on off and angling into the batsman, it misses the defensive bat of Jennings and strikes him on his pads.

Mike Atherton on air explains how Morkel kept Cook nagging around that off stump channel. He set him up nicely. He kept him on strike for most of the time without giving him an easy single, beating his bat numerous times eventually. Cook got consumed by a delivery which was bowled a tad fuller, that went on to hit the top of off. He has made the ex-English skipper his bunny in Tests, getting him out 11 times.
Fuller ball bowled on off, pushed back defensively off the front foot.
Length ball on off, played to the off side.
Length ball outside off, the batsman plays and misses.
Beaten! That was a seaming ball on a length on off and went a tad away from the batter.
Another ball outside off travels into the keeper's gloves.
That ball outside off is left alone.
Length ball on off defended from within the crease.
Length ball outside off, shouldered arms to.
FOUR! Shot! That was full outside off, Westley drives that past the diving extra cover fielder for a glorious boundary. That would surely set his dangling nerves straight.
Full ball on middle, defended off the front foot.
Fuller ball on middle, clipped off the inner half to mid-wicket for a run and Westley gets going.
That was outside off, he left it alone.
Brilliant ball to get first up. Length ball outside off moved away late past the outside edge of his bat.
Tom Westley finds himself at the crease at the fall of the first wicket.

OUT! WHAT A PEACH! 'Alas'tair departs! That was a good length ball that pitched on off and straightened. Cook played for the initial angle of the ball and couldn't adjust to the late movement, only to find the timber disturbed! That was a very good ball, good enough to get a class batsman like the former skipper. It's the 11th time that Cook has fallen to Morkel in Tests. England lose one early in the piece.
Length ball outside off and angling into him, Alastair shoulders arms to that.
Length ball on off, played towards point.

FOUR! That was bowled on a length just outside off,  Jennings pushed his bat at that. The ball took the outside half of the bat and went from the right of gully. Bavuma gave it a spirited chase and just got his foot on the ball as he tried to stop that. Umpires check it upstairs. The replays show that the ball has just kissed the boundary cushions and the dangerous attempt results in nothing good for the fielding side.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Bowled on a length going across him, he shoulders arms to that one.
Length ball on middle, defended off the front foot.
Back of a length ball on leg, Jennings plays it off the back foot. The ball takes his gloves, hits his thigh pad and lobs to where short leg would have been.
This time he lets that ball outside off go through to the keeper.
Back of length ball outside off, Cook pushes his bat out and gets beaten again.
Good ball, almost like the one that got Rabada. It started off back of a length on off and straightened away after pitching. Cook prodded his bat yet the ball evaded it and went through to de Kock.
Fullish ball on off, driven straight to mid off.
Full on off and middle, flicked away in front of square on the leg side.
Full and very much outside off, Cook shoulders arms. There was some lateral movement after the ball passed the stumps.
Morkel to continue from the other end.
Length ball on middle and leg, it strikes him on the thigh pads.
FOUR! STREAKY YET AGAIN! Full ball on off and middle, Keaton goes for the drive. He inside edges that through his legs and the ball rushes down to the fine leg boundary.
Length ball on middle, flicked away on the leg side for a run.
Full ball on off and middle, Cook defends it off the front foot and inside edges that on to the ground.
Length ball defended solidly off the back foot.

Starts off with a full ball on leg, as Jennings misses the flick, he gets hit on the pads. There was a hint of inswing there. That draws appeal from the bowler. They sneak in a leg bye as the ball rolls towards backward square leg.
The players have made their way out as the rain has relented, and yes, Philander is among them too! Cook and Jennings with the bat and it will be the big Vern with the ball to start.
... DAY THREE, SESSION TWO ...

Philander's fitness remains a concern for the visitors as he has always been a standout bowler for them. Morkel and Rabada need to take up the responsibility and rise to the occasion. Conditions are favorable for swing bowling. The tourists need to make the most of it to claw back into the contest. Join us for the second session, as and when the weather permits.

The morning session belongs to South Africa but England are still in the driver's seat with a 198-run lead! The lower order of the Proteas added handy runs to avoid the follow-on and then their bowlers have been on the money with the new ball. Alastair Cook and Keaton Jennings have managed to survive the tricky period before lunch but not before the latter survived a scare. Dean Elgar was the man who dropped him on 6. The youngster has looked jittery in the middle but needs to battle on. The ex-English skipper will look to play another solid knock to take the game further away from South Africa.

Philander is back on the field. Meanwhile, the umpires are having a discussion. They decide that the rain is persistent enough to force the players off the field. So, LUNCH HAS BEEN TAKEN 16 minutes early. Let's hope that the weather clears out.
Cook points his bat skywards as he lets that length ball outside off go to the keeper.
Back of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Length ball down the leg side, Cook goes for the flick and misses.
Length ball outside off, left alone.

FOUR! STREAKY YET EFFECTIVE! Full ball outside off, Cook pushes his bat out. The ball takes the outside edge of his bat and goes between the slip cordon and gully for yet another boundary towards third man.
Length ball outside off, Cook plays and gets beaten there.
Philander is walking off the field.

FOUR! DROPPED! What have you done, Elgar! That's a good length ball on off, Jennings pokes at it as he did in the first innings. The ball takes the outside edge and flies to the right of third slip fielder, who gets a hand on to that but fails to latch on. He didn't look to be in a good position there. The ball goes through to the third man fence for a boundary. That's like rubbing salt on the wounds.
FOUR! Length ball outside off, Jennings hangs out his bat out in defense. He ends up getting an inside edge and the ball misses the stumps and races away to the fine leg boundary.
Another ball outside off left alone.
The rain has got heavier now. The raincoats and umbrellas come out in the crowd. Let's hope it is a passing shower. The artificial lights have been switched on as well.
Length ball outside off, left alone. Good judgement there by the batsman.
A tad fuller outside off, Keaton doesn't bother playing.
Back of a length ball on off and middle, defended from the crease.
Length ball on middle, played towards mid-wicket.
Full ball outside off, Cook drives it though covers for a brace.
Length ball outside off, Cook lets it go.
Full ball outside off, played towards point. A slight misfield allows them a single.
Wide outside off, left alone.

FOUR LEG BYES! Rubbish ball on his pads and punished. Bowled round the wicket angling down the leg side, Keaton had to just tickle it past fine leg. The ball takes his pads and rolls away to the fence for four leg byes.
Length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
A bit of rain is in the air.
Full ball on middle and leg, Cook tries to play it on the on side and gets an inside edge on to the pads.
Fuller ball on off, pushed towards cover.

Lucky way for Jennings to get off a pair! Length ball played towards mid-wicket, The fielder there, Maharaj, has a shy at the non-striker's end, where Kuhn fails to collect it. It was an unnecessary throw there, as it would have benefiting to have Jennings on strike instead of allowing him a run like this. They take a single, England and Jennings get going.
Length ball on middle, driven towards mid off.
Jennings is standing a foot outside the batting crease, a significant change from where he was in the first innings.
Starts off with a good length ball on off and middle which is pushed defensively back.
Vernon Philander is fit enough to share the new ball for the Proteas and will do so.
Full ball sliding down the leg side, it hits Cook on his pads as he misses the flick.
Cook points his bat skywards to that full ball outside off.
Fuller ball on off, played towards mid-wicket. Jennings wanted a run there but slips slightly, no harm done.
Fuller this time, but away from the stumps that doesn't invoke any interest from Alastair.
Length ball outside off, Cook starts his leaving game.
Wow! What a start! Back of a length ball on off and seaming away just a tad. It gets Cook squared up and the ball hits him on the thigh and rolls over towards the slip cordon.
